chapter: 1977: Kansas City honor and the piano
title: His piano limitations and the Basie use of space
summary: Basie says he plays little because he is limited; Kuehl suggests he hears space, which opened up room for the bass.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: : All right, so then I come back to my question, before the singers, which is, how come you like a lot of piano when you're listening to somebody but you don't play a lot of piano yourself?
Cause I can't.
: What does that mean?

That's just purely, because I'm scared. I am limited in what I can play on piano. I thought about this a long time. I thought about this years ago, about how much I can play and how much I can't play, how much to be able to play in the years to come to be around.
So I hadn't thought about me being in competition or -- the piano player in the number one slot.
: So in other words you're telling me -- you're telling me that you decided way back when in ancient history, right.
That's right.
: As opposed to recent history, of 25 years ago.
Right.
: Okay. You decided that you knew
what your limitations were?
That's right.
And so you decided to do, not to play with the band. Is that what you're telling me? That that was your ticket.
What do you mean?

I mean I just don't believe you or let me put it this way, I don't -- although I don't question that this is the way you see it, but I have to interpret it differently, though you may think it's presumptious of me to interpret it differently, I do interpret it differently and I interpret it this way:

I interpret it that that's the way you heard music. It wasn't that you couldn't play a lot of it, but you heard a lot of space. You heard a lot of space and it wasn't that you couldn't play in the spaces and fill in, it's just that that's not the way you heard it.
And, therefore, as a result -- you know space, right.
I heard that before somewhere.
Like three days ago or something.
Well, listen, Bill, when I said space, I know that you say, oh, forget space, but still it's --
It's all right.
I know it's all right.
If it's used right. A lot of people
the way you're playing.
Most everybody is playing left hand --
Playing a lot of right hand.
I mean there's guys, like Pete. Pete and Tom both, they both play -- they're two hands.
Which Pete, you mean Oscar?
Yeah.
Yeah, but you came along at a certain time.
According to what type, what style piano they play, sweetheart.

I understand what you're saying, but I am also saying it changed a whole way of playing at a time. I mean, let's say, if we could say 1935 as a date that's as convenient, let's say there was a whole new way of hearing music and a whole new way of playing piano as original, and you changed the direction, you opened it up, you opened up for the bass, that was original, wasn't it, to open up for the bass.
Now, would you disagree with me?
I don't know I disagree with you when we talk about piano, why should we talk about piano.
We could talk about how you play drums.
You really could now.
